reason: Confirmed, and the numbers hold to a decimal. Driven in chromium at ?v=light&state=quiet across 1440/1280/768/390 with the entrance settled. Mechanism as described: lately.html:374-375 anchors .fortnight at left: calc(var(--x) * 1%) inside .strip and hangs its label at left: var(--gap-tight) with white-space: nowrap and no counter-anchor, and nothing in the relayout pass (lately.html:1038-1069) touches it. The quiet scope's oldest job is 12 (fixture.js), so D.axisMax = max(5, ceil(14/5)*5) = 15 (lately.html:617) and D.fortnight = 14 puts the rule at 93.333% of the strip. Measured, label box 83.5px wide in Geist Mono uppercase: 1440 — strip right 1265, label right 1288.6, card right 1290, so it overhangs the strip by 23.6px and stops 1.4px short of the card's own border with none of the 24px padding every sibling respects; 1280 — identical, label right 1208.6 against card right 1210; 768 — label right 749.8 against card right 720, so 29.8px of it is painted on the page ground outside the white card; 390 — label 337.5 to 421.0 against card right 366 and viewport 390, so it clears the card by 55px and is then guillotined by .scroll's overflow-x: hidden (.scroll scrollWidth 421 vs clientWidth 390). The screenshot at 390 reads exactly 'A FORTN', floating off the card. This is not a fixture edge: the escape triggers whenever the oldest open job is close to a fortnight, which is the state the strip exists to reassure about. The two adjacent gate rules do miss it, verified in source: interaction-check.mjs:627 collects only '.plot .gridline b, .plot .record-tag, .plot .bar-val' and tests them against '.card.hero' (:644), and :867 collects only '.strip-scale span' (:884). The universal 'no sideways scroll' floor (:88-91) reads documentElement.scrollWidth, which is 390 at 390 precisely because .scroll clips first, and 'no silent text clipping' (:134-153) skips .scroll because it holds no direct text node. So the surface is 421px wide inside a 390px clip and every gate is green. Not a re-file of fortnight-marker-lands-beside-a-fifteen-day-tick (r1): that claim was about the rule being mistaken for a 15d tick and was killed on the consequence; this is the label's box leaving its container, a different mechanism with a measured overflow. Note for the record that the r1 refuter's own sharpenedFix proposed right-anchoring this label and only the .strip-scale half of it shipped, so the anchor was left open by an accident of scope, not by decision. Severity: the seat's 'defect' is the right class and I would not raise it. The threshold's meaning survives elsewhere — .dot.old paints accent past the line, the KPI card counts it, and the sr paragraph states it — so the product asserts nothing untrue; it is visibly wrong and passable, not misleading. The proposed fix is also right in mechanism, place and CSS: I applied '.fortnight[data-flip] span { left: auto; right: var(--gap-tight) }' with a strip-box test in the live page and the label lands at 1105.6-1189.1 (1440), 566.8-650.3 (768) and 238.0-321.5 (390), inside the strip at every width, colliding with no .dot and no .strip-scale span, and .scroll's scrollWidth drops from 421 to 390 at 390. Testing against the strip's box is exactly correct rather than the card's, because the strip's left/right edges already sit on the card's content box (231/1265 against a card of 206/1290 with 24px padding and a 1px border). It needs two lines it does not state, given in sharpenedFix; that is a sharpening, not a correction, so this confirms.
sharpenedFix: Take the fix as proposed and add two things it leaves out. (1) Reset before measuring, the pattern measureReading already uses at lately.html:1057-1062: inside relayout(), f.removeAttribute('data-flip'); then measure span.getBoundingClientRect().right against strip.getBoundingClientRect().right + 0.5 and re-set it. As written the attribute is only ever added, so once a resize flips the label it stays flipped at widths where it would fit — invisible on the shipped fixtures (in quiet the flip is needed at every strip width up to 1372px, and in full it is needed below 133px, so neither crosses the boundary) but live the moment a derived axis lands mid-range, e.g. oldest 17 gives axisMax 20 and a rule at 70%, which needs the flip below a 305px strip and not above it. (2) Guard the flipped side too — clamp so a flipped label cannot pass strip.left — even though no current axis can put the rule far enough left to trigger the flip and far enough left to overrun, because the whole class of defect here is an anchor with only one bound. Order matters: run it inside the existing relayout(), after deswarm(), so it re-runs on fonts.ready and on resize; the label's width is font-dependent (83.5px in Geist Mono, different in the fallback face) and a measurement taken against the fallback is a measurement of a page nobody sees. Then close the gate that let this through: widen interaction-check.mjs:884 from '.strip-scale span' to '.strip-scale span, .fortnight span' so the assertion becomes 'nothing in the strip leaves the strip', and assert .scroll.scrollWidth <= .scroll.clientWidth + 1 alongside the documentElement check at :88-91, since the document-level test is blind to anything .scroll clips.
breaks: Low blast radius — one attribute, one CSS rule, one measurement inside a pass that already runs three times. What it can break: (a) the flipped label sits on the same top:0 row as nothing else today, but it now occupies the 84px immediately left of the rule, which is where a dot would sit for an age of roughly axisMax minus four days; the dots are 32px lower in a 92px strip so they do not collide at any width I measured, but deswarm() raises the strip's min-height by 20px per extra row and a dense strip pushes rows upward toward the label, so re-run the collision check at maximum swarm; (b) tooltips are position:fixed off the dot, unaffected; (c) the loading state hides .fortnight with visibility:hidden (lately.html:460), which still returns a real rect, so the measurement is valid there — confirm it does not throw when .fortnight is absent, which it is on first-run, empty and error (D.showsFortnight is false), so guard the querySelector. Re-measure after it lands: interaction-check.mjs 'no age tick leaves the strip' and 'every age tick stands on its own value' at all four viewports (unchanged, but they share the strip box); the universal 'no sideways scroll' floor, which should now pass with real slack at quiet@390 instead of passing on a clip; audit.mjs for ink-3 label contrast, since the label now composites over the card's paper at every width rather than over the page ground at 768 and 390 — the same token, but the backdrop it is scored against changes; and re-shoot quiet at 390/768/1280/1440 in both light and dark, plus full and partial and loading, since the strip renders in all of them and the shots are the record.
